name: 01_exact_diversity
caption: Exact raw-string diversity at the 24 observed rounds. The vertical axis is restricted to make small changes visible; 1,000 trajectories were observed each time.

name: 02_collision_probability
caption: Unordered equal-output pairs divided by N(N−1)/2, scaled to one million pairs. Pair comparisons are not independent experimental replicates.

name: 03_largest_groups
caption: Largest three group sizes at each observation. Ranks can refer to different sentences and members at different rounds; ties use lexical string order.

name: 04_entropy_diversity
caption: Entropy of empirical English output labels and Hill diversity numbers. These are not estimates of retained information about the original sentence.

name: 05_rank_frequency
caption: Empirical rank-frequency profiles, dominated by singleton outputs. A logarithmic rank axis exposes the few repeated outputs; no power-law model is fitted.

name: 06_cluster_size_distribution
caption: Singleton counts and counts of each nonsingleton group size, separated to avoid hiding the small collision groups.

name: 07_normalization
caption: Raw Unicode, NFC, collapsed whitespace, case folding, and punctuation-to-space comparisons. Normalization-induced equality is not semantic equivalence.

name: 08_active_vs_english
caption: Active linguistic states use both language and raw text and are available at all 101 checkpoints. English observations use a different representation space at only the displayed observation rounds.

name: 09_projection_collisions
caption: English-equal pairs split into identical and distinct pre-observation states. This is an operational partition, not a causal estimate of diagnostic translation effects.

name: 10_collision_persistence
caption: Pair persistence across successive observed endpoints. Intervals are 1, 1, 1, 2, then 5 rounds; undefined values when no previous collisions exist are left blank. Shading is a conditional null interval, not a confidence interval.

name: 11_partition_dynamics
caption: Merge/split counts and turnover between the largest groups at successive observations. Tied largest groups are selected lexicographically; the heatmap does not imply a single persistent dominant sentence.

name: 12_semantic_drift
caption: Normalized MiniLM cosine to the corresponding original. Whole trajectories are resampled with the same 500 draws across rounds; bootstrap intervals describe corpus sensitivity, not uncertainty across models or independent experiments.

name: 13_semantic_pair_distribution
caption: Pair-similarity summaries use the same 50,000 sampled distinct trajectory pairs at every observation. The mean is also calculated exactly over all pairs; pair quantiles are descriptive and not independent replicates.

name: 14_semantic_geometry
caption: For unit vectors, dispersion equals one minus squared centroid norm. These are related geometric descriptions, not independent evidence of semantic convergence.

name: 15_embedding_dimension
caption: Eigenvalues of centered embedding covariance determine participation ratio, effective rank and PCA variance shares. These are finite-sample properties of this embedding model, not dimensions of language.

name: 16_semantic_grouping
caption: Exact collision rates compared with semantic similarity, and largest similarity-graph components at three thresholds. Graph connectivity can chain dissimilar sentences and is not an equivalence relation on meaning.

name: 17_sentence_lengths
caption: Word counts and length ratios; shaded region gives trajectory 10th–90th percentiles. Repeated outputs can increase lengths, so shortening is not presumed.

name: 18_lexical_retention
caption: Vocabulary and approximate content retention. Number/date averages include only originals containing those markers; dates use English month names and years, and content words exclude a fixed stop list.

name: 19_quality_flags
caption: Recorded warnings and separately defined heuristic flags. Warning sets overlap. The collector accepted these outputs with status ok; they are not retrospectively relabeled as explicit failures.

name: 20_language_associations
caption: The 15 target languages with highest descriptive flag rates. Input histories and scripts differ, and this is not a causal ranking of language quality.

name: 21_candidate_outputs
caption: Frequency histories for the five outputs with highest peak membership, tied by total contributing trajectories. Exact texts and membership evidence are in candidate_attractors.csv; none is asserted to be an attractor.

name: 22_filtering_robustness
caption: Primary metrics alongside flagged-output and largest-group exclusions. Filtering changes the population and is a sensitivity analysis, not a correction to the observed experiment.
